run: g0_variant_weakness_sweep (21 existing OP6-OP12 variants, map_a, discovery)
reason: Official Aquaticus rules permit a single eligible defender to tag and enforce an interval between successful tags. The current simulator requires two simultaneous taggers (gpu_env/_core/_rules.py:97-98, hardcoded 'pressure >= 2') and has no cooldown. Variant results under this configuration are not evidence about strategy diversity in the Aquaticus-faithful task.

rule_divergences_found.tag_cooldown: ABSENT -- no tag_cooldown / minimum interval anywhere in the codebase
rule_divergences_found.nearest_eligible_target: ABSENT -- all targets under pressure are tagged, so a teammate cannot absorb a tag to protect the carrier
rule_divergences_found.one_second_group_channel: PRESENT (tag_channel_seconds=1.0) -- not in the official per-request eligibility model; simulation approximation
rule_divergences_found.return_home_after_tag: present (nav target overridden to home flag)
rule_divergences_found.safe_flag_return: present (capture requires untagged at home; tag drops flag)

strategic_consequence: In 2v2, 'pressure >= 2' means a lone defender can neither tag nor suppress. One defender is strictly dominated: it forfeits half the offense and buys no defense. There is no intermediate posture, hence no commitment cost, hence a single non-dominated policy. This is consistent with G0's measured fingerprints (num_attackers ~1.0, num_defenders ~0.17-0.27 against all seven base opponents) and plausibly explains the collapse of RUSH/SPLIT/TURTLE/ESCORT into one generalist.

partial_data.usable_as: historical baseline for RULESET_V1 only; NOT evidence about the Aquaticus-faithful task

successor: RULESET_V2 correction, then a fresh map_a incumbent G0-v2 trained from scratch
